newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair sees hopeful signs in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair sees hopeful signs in Northern Ireland.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said there were signs that Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA, was serious about seeking a negotiated solution to the troubles in Northern Ireland.
Blair expressed cautious optimism about the peace process in an interview published on Tuesday in The Mirror newspaper following a new Irish Republican Army ceasefire announced this month.
"...That (the ceasefire) at least is proof that there is some serious intent and desire by Sinn Fein to pursue the democratic path," he said.
Blair also praised the key pro-British Northern Ireland Protestant leader, David Trimble, for continuing to take part in multi-party peace talks.
The talks, to resume in earnest in September, are an attempt to find a lasting settlement to a sectarian conflict that has killed 3,200 over the last 28 years.

Sinn Fein shares the IRA's goal of an end to British rule of Northern Ireland, an aim bitterly opposed by the Protestant community. But Blair said the vast majority of people in the province wanted a lasting peace.
"...The people of Northern Ireland desperately want a lasting political settlement and it is possible to have it because everyone knows what we need in Ulster," he said.
"We need some form of devolved government and some form of north-south cooperation. And those two things are bascially there."
